messages:
Maria Santos: FYI received a high-priority ticket from Bluehaven — they report intermittent 429s and auth errors since 03:15 UTC, and an unexpected billing spike for their dedicated pool. Customer claims baseline ~120 QPS and saw peaks ~900 QPS during campaign.
Jamal Reed: Can you paste the original error snippets from the customer? 429s could be auth or pool saturation. :eyes:
Maria Santos: customer pasted this in the ticket: `{\"error\":\"rate_limited\",\"message\":\"request queued - ded-pool saturated\"}` and `auth: token_rejected` in a separate call. They say most errors coincide with peak windows and some internal retries amplified traffic.
Nina Park: Bluehaven is on a reserved dedicated pool (pool-id: bhv-7). Their contract committed capacity looked right but usage graphs show sustained 75-85% GPU utilization and a few short saturations at ~98% around peaks.
Lucas Chen: That utilization suggests the pool is undersized for their burst profile. Need both right-sizing and autoscale tuning (scale-out cooldowns, burst capacity). Do we have their autoscale policy? Maria?
Maria Santos: Attached from customer: `min_instances: 2, max_instances: 6, scale_policy: cpu_threshold` (they're on older automatic policy). They were expecting burst to 12 with the burst capacity add-on but it wasn't applied — looks like a billing attribution issue flagged by BillingBot.
BillingBot: Billing note: Bluehaven's burst add-on failed to attach on 2026-02-28 due to a billing token mismatch; charges were not provisioned, so cap stayed at 6 instances. I've opened a charge-fix and can reattach once SRE approves a retroactive grant.
Jamal Reed: Ok — two problems: (1) pool mis-sized for QPS spikes, (2) burst add-on didn't attach so autoscale couldn't reach expected headroom. Short term: can we enable temporary overprovisioning for them and pin traffic to other spare capacity? Long term: adjust instance targets.
Lucas Chen: Short-term plan: 1) Move routing rule to prefer spare dedicated nodes in us-west-2 for bhv-7 during their next campaign window; 2) Increase min_instances to 4 and max_instances to 12 for 1 hour windows; 3) Reduce scale-out cooldown to 30s and enable instant-burst for one cycle. I can do 1 and 2 if eng-oncall gives thumbs up.
eng-oncall-bot: @oncall-eng notified. Please include request id and ETA for change rollout.
Maria Santos: Repro steps requested by Lucas from the customer to validate: 1) run this synthetic load from us-west-2: ```bash
# run 10 minute ramp test
siege -c 250 -t10M -d1 -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" https://api.redwood.example.com/v1/generate
``` 2) capture first 2 minutes of stderr and the `/metrics` export from the pool manager. 3) include sample request IDs for a failing call.
Nina Park: Bluehaven agreed to run the ramp test in a 30-minute maintenance window tomorrow 04:00-04:30 UTC. They also sent CSV of their historical QPS: baseline 110-130 QPS weekdays, daily marketing peak 600-900 QPS for ~6–9 minutes, and occasional 1.2k QPS spikes lasting <60s.
Jamal Reed: For sizing guidance, recommend sustained target utilization ~60% (p95) and headroom for instantaneous bursts ~50% — that implies max_instances 12–14 for their 1.2k spikes depending on instance type. Let's pick a conservative target: max_instances=16 to be safe while we tune.
Lucas Chen: Agree on 60% p95. For their hardware profile (A40-equivalent), one instance handles approx 80 QPS at p95 when running chat + kv-cache warm. Calculation: 1200 QPS / 80 ≈ 15 instances -> with 60% target -> 25 instances? wait recalculating: if 1 instance capacity at p95 = 80, to achieve 60% utilization we need instances = ceil(1200 / (80*0.6)) = ceil(1200/48)=25. That's larger than expected because chat + long context reduces per-instance QPS.
Maria Santos: Customer said many requests are short completions (avg tokens small) but they have some long-context flows. Can we recommend mixed routing: pin short-completion traffic to smaller quantized model variants and long flows to dedicated larger instances? That would reduce instance pressure.
Jamal Reed: Good idea — recommend model-splitting and prefix-caching; Redwood Optimize can suggest quantization settings for their workload. Action: send Bluehaven a config snippet and a runbook for routing.
Maria Santos: Draft runbook snippet I posted to the ticket: ```yaml
routing:
  - match: "request.metadata.type == 'short'"
    route_to: bhv-7-small
  - match: "request.metadata.type == 'long'"
    route_to: bhv-7-large
autoscale:
  min_instances: 4
  max_instances: 25
  cooldown: 30s
  instant_burst: enabled
```
Lucas Chen: Before we flip anything, I need these: (A) customer-provided failing request ids, (B) metrics export from their pool for the last 24h, (C) kernel/GPU driver logs for any OOMs. Also ask billing to reattach burst add-on retroactively so we can test full capacity.
BillingBot: Retro-attach queued. Please confirm approval code `RB-ATTACH-142` in this thread to push through.
Nina Park: Approved. Please proceed with retro-attach and send estimate of any prorated charge to customer finance.
Maria Santos: tagging follow-ups: @Jamal I'll schedule the maintenance tomorrow and coordinate the change window. @Lucas once eng-oncall confirms, we'll do the temporary increase + routing tweak. I'll collect the request IDs during the ramp test.
Jamal Reed: I'll prepare a short customer-facing summary with expected timelines and recommended config. Also include link to KB: https://redwood.example.com/kb/dedicated-warmup-and-sizing (customer docs).
Lucas Chen: One more note — add a short-term guard: set per-tenant qps cap at 1.5k and enable exponential retry backoff in client to avoid retry storms. That should reduce retry amplification.
Maria Santos: Thanks all. I'll update ticket with test window results and attach Bluehaven's CSV when they share. :thumbsup:
eng-oncall-bot: Change request logged: CR-2289012345-1. Oncall ETA: 20 minutes.
Maria Santos: closing loop here for now, will update after tests complete.
